text:
River,

Monday morning fact, because you're going to need something to survive the week and I am fundamentally useless in every way except this one:

When NASA launched the Voyager probes in 1977, they included a golden record — a sort of mixtape for the universe. Greetings in fifty-five languages. Whale songs. Chuck Berry. Carl Sagan wanted to include 'Here Comes the Sun' but EMI wouldn't license it. So somewhere past the edge of our solar system, there's a record hurtling through interstellar space that has Azerbaijani greetings and whale songs and Johnny B. Goode, but not the Beatles, because copyright law is apparently a force that transcends the boundaries of human civilisation.

If I were making one, I'd put your laugh on it. Not the polite one. The real one — the one that catches you off guard.

I love you. More than I love the Voyager programme, and I love the Voyager programme quite a lot.

Gale
